papers.title: FutureWorlds: Learning Robotic World Models from Alternative Futures
papers.abstract: Robotic world models predict action-conditioned future scenes, providing a foundation for understanding action outcomes. However, turning alternative predictions into useful learning signals remains challenging: similar candidates limit informative quality comparisons, while diverging trajectories require persistent maintenance of their individual histories. We introduce FutureWorlds, a framework that unifies candidate construction, history maintenance, and learning from relative quality. Built on a multimodal discrete autoregressive model, FutureWorlds uses diverse beam search during reinforcement learning to construct candidate futures that balance confidence and diversity. Candidate-specific bounded memory preserves scene states and ensures that generation and policy scoring use matching histories. We further propose MemSPO (Memory-Conditioned Search-Guided Policy Optimization), which converts video trajectory rewards into group-relative advantages to optimize the world model. On RT-1, BridgeV2, and RoboCasa, FutureWorlds reduces LPIPS for 32-frame predictions by 14.78%, 20.84%, and 9.12%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline on each dataset. Under fixed evaluation configurations, only 200 MemSPO updates further improve generation quality and support continued prediction beyond the training horizon. Memory ablations, decoding sensitivity analysis, and optical-flow evaluation show that these gains extend beyond visual quality to more accurate motion prediction and more consistent object states. Project page and code: https://github.com/Alexander-wu/FutureWorlds.

papers.title: Calibration-risk routing for controlled world-model adaptation
papers.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can exploit simulated experience, but a simulator-to-target shift creates a model-selection problem: correcting the simulator and fitting the target directly can each fail under limited target data. We introduce the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM), which separates initial target data into disjoint fit, selection, and calibration partitions and deploys the family with lower standardized calibration risk. A learned confidence signal and deterministic validity predicates weight one-step imagined policy updates without rewriting physical rewards. We evaluate 540 unique reported run cells across three controlled Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact (MuJoCo) shifts; one exact-routing cell was repeated after a pre-deployment artifact gate, giving 541 completed executions.

papers.title: In CEM, a World Model Is Also a Proposal Mechanism
papers.abstract: The cross-entropy method (CEM) uses world-model scores to select action sequences and fit the distribution sampled in its next iteration. A scoring error can therefore change both the present decision and the candidates considered later. We evaluate these two roles separately. Four types of predictive model generate CEM traces, and every model rescores every saved candidate pool. Executing the same candidates in the environment provides a reference elite set and proposal update.   Across twelve independently trained task-seed units on Walker and Cheetah, the pre-specified proposal distance falls from the first to the final CEM iteration in every unit. Proposal widths contract and fitted means separate relative to the remaining search width. Pairwise ranking agreement stays near chance on Walker and declines on Cheetah; elite-set agreement does not improve. This comparison shows greater variation between scorers than between pool sources on Cheetah; Walker has variation in both and in their pairings. We use the original six units to select Random nonlinear for a one-update intervention, without inspecting intervention outcomes. Replacing its first model-ranked update with an environment-ranked update lowers final realised selected-sequence cost in those six units and in six further units held out from the selection.

papers.title: Block Optimism for Nonstationary Bandits with Latent Linear Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study an endogenous nonstationary stochastic bandit problem with latent linear dynamics, where actions affect both immediate rewards and the future evolution of an unobserved latent state. Rewards are bilinear in the current action and latent state, inducing history-dependent rewards and a nontrivial long-horizon planning problem. The existing explore-then-commit approach achieves $\tilde{O}(T^{2/3})$ regret by uniformly exploring to estimate the latent dynamics and then committing to an optimized open-loop action sequence. We show that this rate can be improved via adaptive block-level optimism. Our key step is a cyclic approximation: under stable dynamics, the infinite-memory reward process can be truncated, and the open-loop benchmark can be approximated by optimizing a finite-memory block-level proxy. Building on this reduction, we propose a UCB-based block algorithm that maintains confidence sets for the truncated dynamics parameters and selects blocks optimistically. We prove a regret bound of order $\tilde{O}(\sqrt T)$, significantly improving over the previous $\tilde{O}(T^{2/3})$ guarantee for the same model. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first $\tilde{O}(\sqrt T)$ regret guarantee for latent linear-dynamics bandits with bilinear reward observations and an open-loop action-sequence benchmark.

papers.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Landweber Iteration with Randomized Normal-Operator Approximation
papers.abstract: Iterative methods are extremely popular for solving linear ill-posed inverse problems. While deterministic convergence, or more precisely, semi-convergence of such methods is widely studied, the problem of quantifying uncertainty in the resulting reconstructions due to random noise in the observed data has received far less attention. In this work, we study uncertainty quantification for the Landweber iteration in linear inverse problems using the Radon transform as a motivating example. We interpret the Landweber reconstruction statistically by analyzing how uncertainty in the measured data is propagated through the reconstruction map. This perspective is closely related to generalized fiducial inference, where uncertainty about the parameter is induced by inverting the relation between the observed data and the unknown (fixed) quantity. We combine the resulting stochastic uncertainty with a theoretical bound on the regularization bias to construct confidence intervals for the reconstructed solution. The evaluation of the resulting uncertainty estimates require repeated operations with the forward operator that can become expensive in large-scale problems. To reduce this cost, we use randomized singular value decomposition to obtain a low-rank approximation of the normal operator associated with the Radon transform and incorporate this approximation in quantifying uncertainty. {In particular, this requires that the additional randomization error introduced due to the use of such randomized techniques be included in our approach for uncertainty quantification.} Numerical results show that the proposed method provides accurate reconstructions and reliable uncertainty estimates at substantially reduced computational cost.

papers.title: Fabrication and microstructural characterization of additively manufactured metal supports for solid oxide fuel cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Porous 430L stainless steel metal supports fabricated by direct metal laser sintering (DMLS) with various designed pore sizes were evaluated for solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) applications. This study reports the metal support properties related to pore size and surface roughness that are critical for defect-free ceramic deposition. The supports were systematically characterized in terms of pore size fidelity and printability, surface pore distribution and roughness, and bridging layer deposition and adhesion relevant to SOFC fabrication and operation. Challenges associated with conventional pore former usage and pore size control were mitigated by designing and printing fine and straight-through pores, while overall porosity was custom-designed and optimized within the printability limit of the DMLS process. Pore size and surface pore distribution were quantified using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) micrographs and image processing techniques. Surface roughness was evaluated using an optical profilometer on bare, polished, gadolinium-doped ceria-coated, and yttria-stabilized zirconia-coated samples. The observed adhesion of the ceramic layers and the improved surface smoothness indicated good compatibility between the additively manufactured metal supports and ceramic coatings, supporting their potential for SOFC applications.

papers.title: Physics-informed Graph Attention-Transformer networks for multi-scale residual displacement prediction in progressive collapse of RC frames
papers.abstract: Nonlinear dynamic finite element analysis (FEA) is the mainstream method for assessing progressive collapse of structures, but its prohibitive computational cost limits rapid evaluation of damaged building systems. This paper proposes a physics-informed Graph Attention-Transformer (GAT-Transformer) framework as an engineering informatics surrogate for predicting residual displacements of reinforced concrete (RC) frames under progressive collapse. The framework transforms structural layouts, initial column-removal scenarios, and physical attributes into graph-based representations, in which beam-column joints are represented as graph nodes, physical beams and columns as graph edges, and slab-aware diagonal connections as virtual edges encoding in-plane slab interactions. A local Graph Attention Network captures neighborhood response redistribution, while a global Graph Transformer with feature bypass learns long-range structural interactions and preserves macro-level descriptors. To address the scale imbalance between horizontal and vertical responses, a decoupled multi-head regression scheme is introduced for multi-scale displacement prediction. Using 9968 parametric cases generated from high-fidelity simulations, the model achieves R 2 = 0.951 on the validation set with an overall MAE of 18.2 mm, reducing MAE by 24.6% relative to GraphGPS. Topology-disjoint testing and extrapolation results further demonstrate spatial generalization across unseen structural configurations and extended structural scales. Validation against a full-scale two-story RC-frame blast test shows good agreement with a relative error of 11.5% in residual displacement. The developed model completes a single-case inference within 5.2 ms and substantially accelerates progressive-collapse response assessment.

papers.title: Recent developments in advanced manufacturing technologies for hernia repair meshes
papers.abstract: Abstract Hernias are one of the most common pathologies, with over 20 million surgeries performed annually worldwide. The most commonly used surgery to treat this pathology involves the implantation of fibrous mesh structures to reinforce weakened abdominal tissue. Although commercially available synthetic and biological meshes have significantly reduced recurrence rates, they are still associated with postoperative complications, such as chronic inflammation, foreign body response, and intra-abdominal adhesions. This review focuses on the use of advanced manufacturing techniques, specifically extrusion-based three-dimensional (3D) printing and electrospinning, in the development of next-generation mesh structures for hernia repair. These techniques offer precise control over structural architecture, customizable mechanical properties, and the ability to integrate bioactive compounds for patient-specific implant design. Furthermore, the combination of extrusion-based 3D printing and electrospinning presents a synergistic approach, utilizing 3D printing for robust mechanical support and electrospinning to mimic the native extracellular matrix (ECM) and regulate the biological interface, ultimately aiming to optimize tissue integration and minimize postoperative complications. In addition to the critical analysis of current advances, this review aims to serve as a practical guide for researchers in this field, providing a structured overview of the reported key parameters and conditions.

papers.title: Patient-Specific Implant Design: Current Evidence for Artificial Intelligence, Imaging and Computational Planning—A Systematic Review of the Biomedical-Indexed Literature
papers.abstract: Background and objectives: Patient-specific skeletal implants are designed through a pipeline of imaging, computational planning and, increasingly, artificial intelligence. Each pillar has its own validation literature, but no review has asked what evidence supports each one in implant design itself. We mapped that evidence from the biomedical-indexed literature in this paper. Methods: A systematic review was conducted under a protocol committed before retrieval (PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, SWiM). MEDLINE, Europe PMC, Crossref and OpenAlex were searched on 2 and 3 September 2026 for primary studies from 2015 onwards applying artificial intelligence, an evaluated imaging pipeline or computational planning to an implant whose geometry derives from the individual patient’s anatomy. Engineering indexes were unavailable, so this review maps biomedical-indexed literature, and a bounded probe was used to estimate what that omits. Two artificial intelligence screeners from different vendors screened every record; every clinical study was appraised twice, independently, by assessors from different vendors. Claims about validation quality are reported on the studies read in full. All screening, charting and appraisals were machine-performed and no human-verified subsample exists. Results: Of 5059 records, 639 studies were included: 373 technical studies, 179 clinical series, 75 comparative studies and 12 randomised trials. Computational planning was applied in 601, an evaluated imaging step in 219 and artificial intelligence in 36. Randomised evidence came from 12 small trials, 10 of them craniomaxillofacial, which evaluated the delivered implant rather than the planning method; virtual surgical planning was used in 11 of them. When restricting to the four studies that measure deviation from the virtual plan, with smaller meaning better, patient-specific implants deviated less from the plan (standardised mean difference −1.21, 95% CI −1.69 to −0.74). Revision or removal was less frequent (3 of 135 against 25 of 149; risk ratio 0.28, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.72); operative time, complications and infection gave intervals compatible with a difference either way. No randomised trial was at low risk of bias, and 69 of 75 comparative studies were at serious risk, mostly of unadjusted confounding, so all estimates are of very low certainty. Among technical studies read in full, independent validation material was used in fewer than half, and files were shared in about one in fourteen. Of 36 artificial intelligence studies, 4 were evaluated on independent data, 2 were used for a real patient, none were clinically comparative, and 8 of 17 cranial studies relied on AutoImplant family benchmarks. Conclusions: The design pipeline is unequally validated: planning has clinical evidence concentrated in one region, computational methods are widely applied but rarely validated independently or shared, and artificial intelligence has benchmark evidence for cranial defect completion and little else. Outcome studies of patient-specific implants should be read as evidence about whole pipelines, and future studies should evaluate the components.

papers.title: Is there a difference in knee biomechanics due to fatigue of the quadriceps versus hamstrings during landing on a single limb? a randomized comparative laboratory study
papers.abstract: The quadriceps and hamstring muscles play a central role in absorbing impact forces and maintaining dynamic knee stability during landing tasks. Together, these muscle groups also strongly influence knee joint kinematics and kinetics. This study aimed to compare the effects of induced fatigue of the quadriceps and hamstring muscles on the kinematics and kinetics of the knee joint during a single-leg landing in a forward-drop jump task. Of the 108 athletes (aged 20–25 years) randomized to either the quadriceps or hamstring fatigue group, 93 completed the study and were analyzed. The peak knee flexion angle, vertical ground reaction force (vGRF), anterior tibial shear force, and knee flexion-extension and abduction-adduction moments were measured before and after inducing fatigue in the quadriceps or hamstrings during a forward-drop jump with a single-leg landing. Hamstring fatigue significantly reduced the peak knee flexion angle ( p < 0.001) compared with quadriceps fatigue. Also, hamstring fatigue significantly increased the vGRF and anterior tibial shear force ( p < 0.001) more than quadriceps fatigue. The peak flexion moment demonstrated a significant Group × Time interaction ( p = 0.022), decreasing significantly following hamstring fatigue ( p < 0.001). Conversely, the peak extension moment showed a significant Group × Time interaction ( p < 0.001), decreasing significantly following quadriceps fatigue ( p < 0.001). The knee abduction and adduction moments were significantly affected ( p < 0.001) by quadriceps fatigue more than by hamstring fatigue. Hamstring fatigue was associated with greater changes in knee flexion angle, vertical ground reaction force, anterior tibial shear force, and peak flexion moment, whereas quadriceps fatigue induced more disturbances in knee abduction and adduction moments. These findings highlight distinct, muscle-specific changes in surrogate biomechanical measures that reflect different mechanical pathways associated with ACL loading. The trial was registered on 5/5/2023, Iranian Registry of Clinical Trial, Identifier: (IRCT20230329057784N1).

papers.title: Patient-specific finite element analysis of immediate loading in the edentulous maxilla: A single-case biomechanical evaluation of three implant configurations
papers.abstract: Abstract Aim: Finite element analysis (FEA) is widely used in implant prosthodontics to assess biomechanical behavior and support treatment planning in complex edentulous cases. This work aimed to evaluate stress distribution patterns associated with three implant configurations (all-on-four, all-on-six, and quad-zygomatic) in the edentulous maxilla using a single patient-specific finite element model under immediate loading conditions. Settings and Design: Two CBCT scans from a single edentulous patient, acquired before and after full-arch bone grafting, were segmented to generate three digital twin models including the maxilla, implants, abutments, and a full-arch prosthesis. Materials and Methods: A unilateral oblique load of 150 N at 45° was applied to the posterior region of the prosthesis using a non-deformable distribution tool to simulate immediate functional loading. Stress distribution and displacement patterns within bone and prosthetic components were evaluated. Statistical Analysis Used: A descriptive biomechanical evaluation based on stress magnitude and distribution patterns was conducted. Results: The simulations demonstrated distinct biomechanical responses among the implant configurations. The all-on-six model showed a more uniform stress distribution with lower peak stress values compared to the other configurations. In this model, the difference between tensile and compressive cortical stress peaks was reduced relative to the all-on-four and quad-zygomatic configurations. In all scenarios, stress values remained within physiological limits reported for bone tissue. Conclusion: Within the limitations of a single patient-specific model and the absence of inferential statistical analysis, this single-case biomechanical evaluation suggests that digital twin–based finite element analysis may serve as an exploratory tool for biomechanical assessment and prosthodontic treatment planning in implant-supported rehabilitation of the edentulous maxilla.

papers.title: Electrospun SLIPS Coatings for Controlled Local Drug Release on Implant Surfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Postoperative inflammatory reactions and bacterial colonization limit the long-term functionality of implantable medical devices, particularly for implants in permanent contact with biological fluids. Integrating drug delivery directly into implant surfaces offers a way to achieve high local drug concentrations while reducing systemic exposure. In this work, electrospun slippery liquid-infused porous surfaces (SLIPS) are evaluated as implant coatings for controlled local drug delivery, with a focus on how different drug loading strategies and lubricant viscosities influence release behavior. Polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofiber mats were fabricated by electrospinning and subsequently infused with silicone oils of different. Anti-inflammatory and antibiotic model drugs (Dexamethasone and Ciprofloxacin) were incorporated either into the polymer fiber matrix or into the infused lubricant phase. Surface properties were characterized by contact and sliding angle measurements, while drug distribution was analyzed using scanning electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy. Drug release was quantified under physiological conditions using UV-Vis spectroscopy. Drug incorporation into the polymer fibers resulted in slower and more homogeneous release profiles, whereas lubricant-based loading led to pronounced initial burst release. Increasing lubricant viscosity reduced cumulative release, indicating an additional diffusion barrier effect. These findings show that electrospun SLIPS coatings can be tailored to achieve distinct release profiles and may be suitable for different implantassociated therapeutic scenarios.

papers.title: VED-dependent HIP densification of PBF-LB Inconel 718: Defect closure thresholds, microstructural homogenization, and nano-mechanical response
papers.abstract: Defining the initial porosity limits within which hot isostatic pressing (HIP) can effectively densify laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) components remains a critical gap for industrial qualification of additively manufactured nickel-based superalloys. This study systematically investigates the influence of volumetric energy density (VED) on initial defect population in Inconel 718 (IN718) and its role in densification response during HIP. Specimens with varying initial porosity (0.01% to 17.76%) were fabricated by intentionally varying laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing. All samples were subjected to identical HIP conditions (1160 °C, 100 MPa, 4 h) incorporating a combined in-situ solution treatment, followed by double ageing in a vacuum furnace. Porosity evolution, pore morphology, microstructural transformations, and nano-mechanical response were characterized before and after HIP. Three distinct densification regimes were identified based on initial porosity. Below 0.1%, the absolute densification benefit is negligible due to argon-filled gas pores resistant to closure. Between 0.1% and 10%, closure efficiencies of 87–98% are achieved, representing the optimal HIP densification window. Between 10% and 17%, the response degrades progressively, and above ~17% densification efficiency becomes negative owing to open-pore network formation and argon gas expansion during subsequent vacuum treatments. Furthermore, HIP at 1160 °C fully dissolved Nb-rich laves phases, eliminated melt pool boundaries, and promoted recrystallization from columnar to equiaxed grain structure. Double ageing produced a uniform distribution of fine γ′/γ″ strengthening precipitates. These findings establish quantitative defect acceptance criteria for pre-HIP qualification of PBF-LB nickel superalloy components, supporting cost-effective post-processing for aerospace and energy applications.

papers.title: Proof-of-concept validation and characterisation of a DLP 3D bioprinted vascularised colorectal cancer model
papers.abstract: Tumor vascularisation is essential in promoting cancer growth and metastasis and represents a key target for efficient drug delivery. Nevertheless, in vitro experimental models are limited to monolayer (co)cultures of endothelial and malignant cells, scratch and transwell migration assays where the vascularisation process is largely neglected. Direct contacts between different cell types and extracellular matrix (ECM) components, and processes like cell migration and invasion and ECM remodeling are also difficult to reproduce using conventional culturing methods. This study aims to address some of these limitations by developing digital light processing (DLP) 3D bioprinted model of colorectal cancer based on methacrylated gelatin (GelMA) and containing endothelialised channels. The materials and approaches proposed here were additionally validated with 3D biofabricated in-house made designs based on the (bio)casting of GelMA and collagen hydrogels, and with 3D printed transwell assays. We found that our DLP bioprinting and 3D biofabrication protocols support the growth of HCT-116 colorectal cancer cells (embedded in the gel) and the survival of HUVEC endothelial cells (seeded to the channels), that cells adhere well to the collagen and GelMA matrices, and that the cells can remodel the hydrogel as revealed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Importantly, we also found that HUVECs migrate through these substrates in both the channel and transwell constructs. Altogether, to our knowledge, this pilot study presents the first DLP bioprinted model of CRC using GelMA, and the only DLP bioprinted colorectal cancer model seeded with HUVECs suitable for in vitro study of tumor vascularisation and drug delivery.

papers.title: Silk biomaterials in the era of digital manufacturing: Physics, processing, and biomedical translation
papers.abstract: Additive manufacturing has gained prominence as a powerful platform for fabricating morphologically complex and functionally active biomaterial constructs for biomedical applications. Among biopolymers, silk has been extensively explored owing to its good mechanical properties (tensile strength 300–740 MPa, Young's modulus 5–17 GPa, toughness ∼70 MJ/m3), degradation behavior, rich functional bioactive groups, and aqueous processability. However, translating silk into printable bioinks is limited by its inherent structural hierarchy and sensitivity to processing conditions. This review provides a critical overview of the properties and processing of silk in light of Digital manufacturing, with emphasis on structure, properties, functionalization, and printability. Moreover, the effects of different degumming methods and functionalization protocols on the rheological properties of silk solutions are analyzed. The resulting implications for printing fidelity are also examined, demonstrating that processing-derived molecular and conformational changes critically determine flow behavior, shape retention, and structural resolution in 3D-printed constructs. State-of-the-art developments in extrusion-based, inkjet, and light-assisted printing techniques for silk-based systems are systematically evaluated, including cross-linking mechanisms, composite formulations, and post-printing analyses, depending on the desired application focus. Moreover, the influence of printing parameters on filament formation, hierarchical organization, and mechanical and functional performance is thoroughly discussed. Crucially, biomedical applications of 3D printed silk constructs spanning from tissue engineering scaffolds, and drug delivery systems to biosensors are reviewed, emphasizing design-function correlation. Thus, this review positions silk as a versatile material for next-generation digital manufacturing and biofabrication.

papers.title: A review study on immediate vs delayed implant loading
papers.abstract: Implant loading protocols have evolved from traditional delayed loading (DL) toward immediate loading (IL) to shorten treatment time and improve patient experience. However, IL introduces biomechanical and biologic risks (micromotion, early marginal bone remodeling, prosthetic overload) that may affect survival and peri-implant tissues, particularly in low-density bone and complex reconstructions.To review contemporary evidence (post-2015 emphasis) comparing immediate versus delayed implant loading in randomized and randomized-like clinical studies, and to provide clinically usable synthesis of outcomes and indications.A focused literature appraisal was performed using peer-reviewed clinical trials and high-quality systematic reviews/meta-analyses evaluating IL versus DL in single-tooth, posterior partial edentulism, mandibular overdentures, and full-arch maxillary rehabilitations. Priority was given to randomized controlled designs and studies reporting implant survival, marginal bone level (MBL) change, peri-implant indices, complications, and patient-reported outcomes. Key outcomes were summarized in structured tables.Across indications, many RCTs show similar implant survival for IL and DL when primary stability is high, occlusal control is appropriate, and patient risk is low. In mandibular Locator-retained overdentures, IL demonstrated similar survival and in some trials less radiographic bone level change compared with DL at 1–5 years. In posterior mandible split-mouth RCT data with >10 years follow-up, IL showed no significant disadvantage versus DL in crestal bone loss. In single-tooth implants (esthetic zone), IL and DL demonstrated comparable esthetic and bone outcomes at 5 years, though smoking status influenced bone loss in at least one RCT. In short implants (posterior maxilla), IL may be associated with higher bone loss and bleeding indices than DL, despite generally acceptable outcomes. For maxillary full-arch fixed prostheses, long-term data suggest comparable survival between IL and DL, with some reports indicating lower mean bone loss in IL groups under specific protocols.IL can be predictable and comparable to DL in appropriately selected cases, but it is more technique- and case-sensitive. DL remains preferable when primary stability is uncertain, parafunction exists, bone quality is poor, systemic or local risk is elevated, or occlusal control cannot be ensured.

papers.title: Acoustic Digital Twin for Prestressed Concrete Bridges
papers.abstract: Prestressed concrete bridges may be susceptible to stress corrosion cracking in tendons, which can result in sudden failure without visible warning signs. Assessment methods are therefore required to identify damage-related structural changes at an early stage. Acoustic emission analysis has proven to be a reliable and cost-effective technique for detecting tendon wire breakages. This research employs digital twin technology to model acoustic wave propagation in concrete bridges and to optimize the design, deployment, and interpretation of acoustic monitoring systems. To establish a reference signal database, several bridges in Germany affected by stress corrosion cracking were investigated, and acoustic emission signals generated by controlled wire cuts were recorded. Digital representations of the bridge structures, including three-dimensional models and finite element meshes, were developed to serve as the foundation of the digital twin. The propagation of elastic waves resulting from wire breakage were simulated using the spectral-element method. A time-reversal technique was applied to localize the acoustic source, thereby supporting decision-making regarding subsequent measures, such as traffic load redistribution. The proposed acoustic digital twin approach thereby contributes to improving the safety of bridges at risk of structural deterioration.

papers.title: Organoidogenesis: modulating morphology and perturbation
papers.abstract: Organoids, three-dimensional (3D) structures derived from stem cells, hold immense promise for disease modeling and regenerative medicine by recapitulating native tissue architecture and function, yet their full potential is often limited by morphological heterogeneity and a lack of precise developmental control. This review provides a comprehensive overview of cutting-edge strategies to modulate and perturb organoid morphology, addressing these critical challenges. The ‘top-down’ bioengineering approaches, including the engineering of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and culture environment, alongside advanced fabrication techniques such as bioprinting that impose external geometric constraints were explored. Further, ‘bottom-up’ strategies that leverage intrinsic biological processes through biochemical and genetic perturbations, such as targeted modulation of key signaling pathways were detailed. Critically, the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven image analysis for robust, high-throughput quantification of morphological outcomes were highlighted. By synthesizing these complementary approaches, this review provides a roadmap for engineering next-generation organoids with enhanced control over form and function, paving the way for more predictive and reliable in vitro systems. An organoid’s physical architecture directly reflects its functional maturity and physiological fidelity. Complex, organized structures often signify a closer recapitulation of the native organ’s in vivo state. Dynamic culture systems, like microfluidics, overcome the nutrient and oxygen limitations of static methods, preventing necrotic cores and promoting the development of larger, more mature organoids. Systematically perturbing organoid development with biochemical, genetic, or biophysical tools is a powerful strategy to dissect the fundamental mechanisms of tissue morphogenesis, organization, and disease pathogenesis. Bioengineering techniques like scaffolding, bioprinting, and ECM engineering guide the stochastic self-assembly of organoids, enabling the formation of predictable and reproducible morphologies with desired functions. Precisely modulating key signaling pathways (e.g., Wnt, BMP) with small molecules is a fundamental bottom-up strategy to control cell fate decisions, differentiation, and emergent architectural organization. AI-driven deep learning models automate image analysis, enabling rapid, objective, and high-throughput quantification of morphology while minimizing human bias and allowing for longitudinal tracking of organoid development.

papers.title: Thermodynamically consistent physics-informed neural network-finite element method for viscoelastic fluids using square-root conformation
papers.abstract: Viscoelastic fluids are commonly found in nature and industry, yet their accurate numerical simulation remains challenging due to complex constitutive relations and numerical instabilities. Here, we propose a hybrid PINN-FEM framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) with the finite element method (FEM) for simulating viscoelastic flows. The proposed method is strictly guided by the general equation for non-equilibrium reversible–irreversible coupling (GENERIC) formalism to ensure thermodynamic consistency and employs the square-root conformation representation to expose the intrinsic low-dimensional structure of the constitutive equations. Specifically, polymer entropy can be expressed as a scalar function of the eigenvalues of the square-root conformation tensor. Leveraging this fact, we transform the constitutive learning task from high-dimensional tensor regression into a simple scalar function approximation, thereby significantly reducing the dimensionality of the learning problem and the required training data size. We validate the method on Poiseuille flow, four-roll mill flow, and the flow around a periodic array of cylinders across a range of Weissenberg numbers. The results demonstrate that as the Weissenberg number increases, the viscoelastic fluids exhibit enhanced elasticity, leading to a nonlinear expansion of the regions covered by the eigenvalues of the square-root conformation tensor. By combining the physical rigor of GENERIC with the data-driven flexibility of PINN and the computational power of FEM, this work provides an efficient, accurate, and thermodynamically consistent approach for developing constitutive models, with promising extensibility to more complex fluid systems.

papers.title: Stress analysis of mandibular implant-supported overdenture retained with bar and ball attachments of different heights: A comparative finite element study
papers.abstract: Abstract Aim: To evaluate and compare stress distribution patterns in mandibular implant-supported overdenture retained with bar and ball attachment systems at two attachment heights (1 mm and 3 mm) using three-dimensional finite element analysis (FEA). Settings and Design: An in silico comparative three-dimensional finite element analysis study. Materials and Methods: Four three-dimensional finite element models of an edentulous mandible restored with two interforaminal bone-level implants (3.5 × 10 mm) were developed. The models incorporated bar attachments with heights of 1 mm (A1) and 3 mm (A2), and ball attachments with heights of 1 mm (B1) and 3 mm (B2). All materials were assumed to be homogeneous, isotropic, and linearly elastic. Complete osseointegration was simulated using bonded contact conditions. A mesh convergence test was performed, and mesh refinement continued until the change in peak von Mises stress between successive mesh refinements was <5%. A static vertical load of 100 N was applied at the central occlusal fossa of the first molar under unilateral and bilateral loading conditions. Stress distribution was evaluated qualitatively and quantitatively using von Mises stress analysis. Statistical Analysis Used: No statistical analysis was performed. Stress distribution was compared descriptively using qualitative stress distribution patterns and quantitative von Mises stress values generated by the finite element models. Results: Under unilateral loading, stresses were concentrated predominantly on the working side, with the implant neck serving as the principal site of stress concentration. Increasing attachment height increased stress magnitudes in both bar and ball attachment systems under unilateral and bilateral loading conditions. Overall, stress concentrations were greatest at the implant neck, followed by the implant body and apical region. Cortical bone consistently exhibited higher stress values than cancellous bone across all models. Conclusion: Within the limitations of this finite element study, attachment height and splinting configuration influenced peri-implant stress distribution. Increased attachment height was associated with greater stress magnitudes in both attachment systems.

papers.title: “Trojan Horse”‐Inspired Bionic Coating of Mesh‐Like Assembled Lysozyme Nanofibers for Anti‐Infection, Anti‐Oxidative Stress and Bone Repair
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bacterial biofilm infection and sustained oxidative stress response seriously affect the osseointegration of bone implants. Here, this study developed a bioactive Mg 2+ loaded tannic acid (TA)/lysozyme amyloid protein fiber (LAPF) composite antioxidative coating to enhance antibacterial, antioxidative and pro‐osteogenic functions of bone implants. Inspired by “Trojan horse”, the mesh‐like TA/LAPF coatings exhibited good antibacterial properties, significantly inhibiting the formation of bacterial biofilms. Interestingly, the TA/LAPF coatings cleared 2,2’‐azino‐bis‐(3‐ethylbenzthiazoline‐6‐sulfonic acid) free radicals obviously (scavenging rate of 83.46 ± 1.43%), and inhibited intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) under an oxidative stress environment. In addition, the biomimetic LAPF coatings exhibited good blood compatibility, promoting the migration of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and angiogenesis effectively. Notably, the (TA/LAPF) 8 +Mg 2+ coatings could effectively improve early adhesion of BMSCs, and exhibited both great in vitro alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity and osteogenic mineralization. In 6‐week implantation experiments, Mg 2+ loaded TA/LAPF coating significantly inhibited in vivo bacterial growth and promoted bone regeneration. The biomimetic mesh‐like coatings of antibacterial protein‐based nanofiber provide important guidance for the design of anti‐infection scaffolds in surface engineering of bone repair.

papers.title: GelMA hydrogels for bone regeneration: Linking clinical scenarios with biofabrication
papers.abstract: Objectives Critical-sized bone defects in cranio-maxillofacial, orthopedic, and dental settings remain difficult to treat because conventional grafts and synthetic substitutes rarely provide simultaneous space maintenance, mechanical stability, and long-term integration. Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) has emerged as a promising hydrogel platform, combining extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived bioactivity with photocrosslinkable chemistry, tunable mechanics, and compatibility with advanced biofabrication. However, most studies still emphasize material synthesis and generic applications rather than configuration for specific clinical environments. This review therefore reframes GelMA-based bone regeneration around the clinical setting in which the scaffold must function. Methods This is a narrative, scenario-driven synthesis rather than a systematic review. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for GelMA-based bone studies, mainly from 2015 onward, and representative work was prioritized when it reported a defined fabrication route and defect-relevant structural, biological, or in vivo outcomes. Results Recent GelMA-based strategies are organized into four clinical scenarios: (i) large or irregular defects needing robust space maintenance and perfusable architectures; (ii) periodontal and maxillofacial defects requiring durable, selectively permeable guided bone regeneration membranes; (iii) post-surgical or open defects with high infection risk that demand sustained local antibacterial and immunomodulatory activity; and (iv) ischemic or irradiated defects, in which pro-angiogenic, antioxidant, and immune-reprogramming functions are essential. We map acellular 3D printing, cell-laden bioprinting, electrospinning, GelMA microgels, and hybrid combinations to scenario-specific design requirements across these clinical settings. We also outline key translational priorities—standardized GelMA synthesis, controlled photocuring, and safety-verified multifunctional composites—to support defect- and scenario-specific bone regeneration. Conclusions By linking clinical need, fabrication strategy, and biological function, this review positions GelMA as a flexible platform for defect- and scenario-specific bone regeneration. Because the synthesis is narrative, the comparative tables are qualitative and not head-to-head benchmarking.

papers.title: FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES OF TOTAL HIP ARTHROPLASTY IN BONY ANKYLOSIS OF THE HIP
papers.abstract: Aim of the study is to assess changes in quality of life, walking speed, periarticular muscle performance and basic functional activity in patients with bony ankylosis of the hip during the 12 months after total hip arthroplasty (THA) performed with the proposed technique compared with the conventional technique. Material and methods. Between 2013 and 2024, 240 patients with stage III–IV hip ankylosis were treated at the Republican Specialized Scientific and Practical Medical Center of Traumatology and Orthopedics. The main group comprised 130 (54%) patients operated on using the proposed technique, and the control group 110 (46%) patients operated on using conventional methods. Detailed functional assessment was performed on all patients using the EQ-5D questionnaire with a visual analogue scale (EQ-VAS), the 10-metre walk test, a 15-second step test and the Barthel Index before surgery, at discharge, and at 3, 6 and 12 months. Results. At baseline the groups were comparable in quality of life (EQ-VAS 59.3 ± 8.0 vs 57.0 ± 9.2; p = 0.47) and walking speed (0.51 ± 0.11 vs 0.44 ± 0.13 m/s; p = 0.12). At 12 months EQ-VAS was 78.5 ± 10.1 in the main group and 67.5 ± 9.2 in the control group (p = 0.004), walking speed was 1.39 ± 0.44 vs 1.05 ± 0.40 m/s (p = 0.04), and the Barthel Index was 85.2 vs 75.0 points. The step test showed faster recovery of operated-limb muscle performance in the main group from postoperative day 15. Conclusion. THA significantly improves quality of life, walking speed and independence in daily living in patients with bony ankylosis of the hip. With the proposed technique, outcomes at 6–12 months were significantly better than with the conventional technique.

papers.title: The influence of part height on the properties and microstructure of AlSi7Mg produced by laser powder bed fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) is an additive manufacturing technology commonly used to manufacture AlSi7Mg components due to its ability to produce customisable parts of complex geometries. While this is true, the geometric factors associated with these complex geometries are often not considered during manufacturing, and as such, this research aims to investigate the influence of part height on the mechanical and microstructural properties of AlSi7Mg. The hardness of the as-built parts was seen to decrease 14.8% from 128 HV near the build plate to 109 HV 250 mm from the build plate. A microstructural analysis revealed that the melt pools, grain structure, and solid solution strengthening all remained consistent over the build height. An increase in residual stress along the build direction from 70 to 223 MPa from the bottom to the top of the build occurred due to in-situ annealing during the manufacturing process. Cells within the grains increased in size from 0.64 µm to 1.01 µm over the build height due to changes in thermal gradient and solidification velocity, reducing their Hall–Petch strengthening effect near the top of parts. Increased formation of solute atom clusters and GP zones was also observed nearer the build plate due to in-situ ageing, contributing to the gradient in hardness values seen over the build height. These results indicate that geometric factors, including the height of a part, need to be properly considered when PBF-LB is utilised, while also highlighting the importance of proper heat treatment as a homogenisation step.

papers.title: Architected LPBF metallic metamaterials with enhanced torsional performance for bionic applications
papers.abstract: The confluence of additive manufacturing, computational design and biomimetic engineering can bring a paradigm change in the metamaterial application space. However, lattice metamaterials have largely been investigated using uniform unit-cell architectures and are often designed agnostic of the dominant loading mode. Under torsion, unlike axial loading, the highest apparent shear stresses occur near the outer circumference; therefore, failure of peripheral load-bearing unit cells can strongly compromise structural integrity. In this study, we present a field-grading methodology to improve the torsional performance of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) Ti–6Al–4V lattice structures. A simple cubic (SC) unit cell was radially graded to obtain a field graded simple cubic (FGSC) lattice with increased material allocation in the high-shear peripheral region while maintaining matched nominal relative density. Under quasi-static torsion, FGSC lattices exhibited up to 30% higher apparent shear strength than uniform SC lattices at matched measured relative density, 22% on average, together with up to 169% longer torsional fatigue life among the tested densities. The structures followed Gibson–Ashby-type power-law scaling, albeit with constants that differ from classical idealized lattices. Finite element analysis showed that radial grading lowers the mean apparent stress amplification relative to an equivalent solid bar and reduces the radially binned 99th-percentile von Mises stress by 18% on average. Principal-stress analysis identified the strut junctions as the fatigue-critical, tensile-constrained sites. Owing to their tunable stiffness, open porosity, and prospective drug-loading capacity, the proposed field graded cellular architectures offer a promising route toward damage-tolerant implantable devices.

papers.title: Experimental Characterisation and Finite Element Modelling of Polyamide-11 Fabricated via Multi Jet Fusion
papers.abstract: HP Multi Jet Fusion (MJF) polyamide-11 (PA11) was characterised experimentally and used to calibrate finite element material models for the quasi-static regime. Characterisation covered tension in six build orientations and compression in three. Validation used threepoint bending at XY and YX, and a vertically aligned triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid. The flat XY orientation was the anisotropy extreme, carrying a tension–compression yield asymmetry of 30.2% that fell to 14.3% at YX and was negligible at XZ. The modulus asymmetry ran the opposite way, 7% at XY against 20% to 27% elsewhere. Elastic-plastic and asymmetric models were calibrated at the representative YX basis, with XY as the constraining case. Single-stress-state fits deviated by up to 7.8% in the other branch, and the tabular tension-only fit failed outright in compression at YX. At YX the fits carrying both branches held both stress states, the asymmetric formulation trading compressive accuracy for tensile, and at XY it alone held both. In three-point bending the asymmetric YX model matched the experiment, while the XY coupons exceeded both XY-calibrated models, an unexplained flexure elevation. In the gyroid crush the leading YX models reproduced the three-phase response, slightly over-predicting the plateau. YX is recommended as the calibration basis, with the combined-hardening elastic-plastic fit as the general-purpose model. The asymmetric formulation should be considered where bending stiffness governs, on the strength of an empirical rather than mechanistic agreement.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural operators for the in situ characterization of locally reacting sound absorbers
papers.abstract: Accurate knowledge of acoustic surface admittance or impedance is essential for reliable wave-based simulations, yet its in situ estimation remains challenging due to noise, model inaccuracies, and restrictive assumptions of conventional methods. This work presents a physics-informed neural operator approach for estimating frequency-dependent surface admittance directly from near-field measurements of sound pressure and particle velocity. A deep operator network is employed to learn the mapping from measurement data, spatial coordinates, and frequency to acoustic field quantities, while simultaneously inferring a globally consistent surface admittance spectrum without requiring repeated evaluations of an explicit numerical forward model during inversion. The governing acoustic relations, including the Helmholtz equation, the linearized momentum equation, and Robin boundary conditions, are embedded into the training process as physics-based regularization, enabling physically consistent and noise-robust predictions. The method is validated using synthetically generated data from a simulation model for two planar porous absorbers under semi free-field conditions across a broad frequency range. Results demonstrate accurate reconstruction of both real and imaginary admittance components and reliable prediction of acoustic field quantities. Parameter studies confirm improved robustness to noise and sparse sampling compared to purely data-driven approaches, highlighting the potential of physics-informed neural operators for in situ acoustic material characterization.

papers.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Methods for Uncertainty Quantification of Tumor Growth Modeled by a Parametric Semilinear Parabolic Reaction-diffusion Equation
papers.abstract: Abstract. We study the application of a quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) method to a class of semilinear parabolic reaction-diffusion partial differential equations used to model tumor growth. Mathematical models of tumor growth are largely phenomenological in nature, capturing infiltration of the tumor into surrounding healthy tissue, proliferation of the existing tumor, and patient response to therapies, such as chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Considerable interpatient variability, inherent heterogeneity of the disease, sparse and noisy data collection, and model inadequacy all contribute to significant uncertainty in the model parameters. It is crucial that these uncertainties can be efficiently propagated through the model to compute quantities of interest (QoIs), which, in turn, may be used to inform clinical decisions. We show that QMC methods can be successful in computing expectations of meaningful QoIs. Well-posedness results are developed for the model and used to show a theoretical error bound for the case of uniform random fields. The theoretical linear error rate, which is superior to that of standard Monte Carlo, is verified numerically. Encouraging computational results are also provided for lognormal random fields, prompting further theoretical development.

papers.title: Tailoring the Surface Performance of Near-β Ti-13Nb-13Zr Alloy Through TaN/Au Bilayer Coatings: Electrochemical Stability, Tribocorrosion Mechanisms and Biocompatibility
papers.abstract: β-Type titanium alloys mitigate stress shielding through their low elastic modulus, but their limited wear resistance restricts their use in articulating surfaces. This study evaluated the effect of a 100 nm Au interlayer on the structural, electrochemical, tribocorrosion and biological behaviour of TaN coatings deposited by magnetron sputtering on aged Ti-13Nb-13Zr. Coatings were characterised by XRD, SEM and AFM and assessed by potentiodynamic polarisation, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and ASTM G119 tribocorrosion tests in Ringer’s lactate at 37 °C, ICP-MS, and MTT and LDH assays with MG-63 cells. Both coatings were columnar and dominated by δ-TaN; the interlayer attenuated the ε-TaN and γ-Ta2N phases and increased the crystallite size from 24 ± 3 to 31 ± 2 nm. The TaN/Au system shifted the corrosion potential from −210 ± 18 to +35 ± 10 mV vs. Ag/AgCl and lowered the corrosion current density 23-fold. Under tribocorrosion, the friction coefficient fell from 0.28 to 0.17, the wear volume fell 7.2-fold and the synergistic fraction fell from 35% to 14%. Ti release fell from 1.85 to 0.16 µg·cm−2 and 72 h cell viability rose from 82 ± 5% to 96 ± 3%. A nanometric noble interlayer is therefore a promising strategy for articulating surfaces of β-titanium alloys.

papers.title: Becoming-with GenAI: reconfiguring agency and authorship in science curriculum development
papers.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the entanglement of researcher’s agency and authorship in curriculum development mediated by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Despite growing enthusiasm for GenAI’s transformative potential, little is known about the process of becoming-with AI in the epistemic and ethical labor of design. Guided by the research question – what forms of agency and authorship emerge through the process of becoming-with AI in AI-mediated curriculum design? Design/methodology/approach Employing a hermeneutic autoethnographic methodology, the researcher documented a lived experience through iterative interactions with GenAI across curriculum planning, sequencing, mapping, alignment and implementation. Data sources included structured prompting protocols, reflective analytic memos and Photovoice artifacts capturing critical decision points in AI-assisted design. Findings Qualitative content analysis has revealed five configurations in curriculum work: GenAI as a mediator of curricular coherence, an architect of sequencing learning, a cartographer of curricular alignment, a curator of contextualized learning experiences and an orchestrator of aligned and active learning. Originality/value Findings indicate that agency and authorship are not diminished in AI-mediated contexts but reconstituted as distributed and ethically intensified practices. GenAI redistributes cognitive labor while amplifying the need for disciplined discernment in evaluating alignment, coherence and epistemic integrity. Curriculum development thus emerges as a negotiated sociotechnical practice in which professional judgment remains the locus of accountability.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Bioprinting Quality Using Integrated Experimental and Computational Data
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting of hydrogel inks is an enabling technology for tissue engineering and the fabrication of personalized drug-delivery systems. However, in most laboratories the extrusion parameters are still optimized by slow, resource-intensive trial-and-error, because printability depends on the combined and often nonlinear influence of ink composition, extrusion pressure, and nozzle geometry rather than on any single variable. Alginate–methylcellulose (Alg–MC) is a widely used pharmaceutical bioink whose shear-thinning behavior makes this optimization particularly demanding. Here we developed a physics-informed machine-learning framework that predicts extrusion print quality before printing. A hybrid dataset of 3280 labeled samples was assembled by combining laboratory extrusion experiments, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of nozzle flow, and controlled augmentation with a deep belief network (DBN). Five physics-informed features encoding pressure-to-diameter and shear-rate interactions were engineered to embed rheological domain knowledge. Five base classifiers alongside two ensemble strategies, seven models in all, were benchmarked under five-fold stratified cross-validation. The voting ensemble performed best (accuracy, 93.3%; F1 = 0.929), narrowly ahead of the stacking ensemble (93.3% accuracy; F1 = 0.928). Alg:MC ratio, extrusion pressure, and the pressure–diameter interaction term stood out as the dominant predictors, consistent with established alginate rheology. On external validation—withholding one composition ratio and one needle gauge entirely from training and testing on those genuinely unseen conditions—accuracy was 75.9%, a stricter test than a random held-out split. Overall, the framework offers a practical, interpretable way to cut down experimental burden in pharmaceutical bioink development.

papers.abstract: MaruDhara – THERMOLIFT is a technical research report documenting a physics-informed decision-support prototype for the coupled optimization of Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS) and Sucker-Rod Pumping (SRP) in a heavy-oil well, developed for Smart India Hackathon 2026 Problem Statement SIH26120 (Oil India Limited). The prototype integrates reservoir, well and surface-response relationships into a single decision workflow, linking steam injection → thermal state → viscosity → inflow/mobility → SRP response → production, energy and risk. The report presents the complete THERMOLIFT framework, including its data and state-estimation layer, reduced-order coupled physics models, CSS–SRP scenario engine, hard-constraint screening, multi-objective ranking, uncertainty and data-quality gating, SRP diagnostics, counterfactual replay, provenance and audit mechanisms, and operator-in-the-loop decision support. A controlled coupled-versus-independent decision experiment is included to examine how jointly evaluating CSS and SRP changes the resulting operating decision. The report also documents sensitivity analysis, temporal validation, physics-consistency checks, current-practice comparison, future deployment pathways, and known model limitations. The prototype uses a representative Baghewala-style synthetic dataset consisting of 2,688 hourly observations across four consecutive CSS cycles. The reported numerical results are therefore synthetic benchmark results and must not be interpreted as measured Baghewala field performance or Oil India-validated results. The system operates in an advisory, human-in-the-loop mode and does not directly control field equipment. The report deliberately documents current limitations, including the absence of field calibration and the failure of the present thermal model to meet its chronological backtesting tolerance. These limitations are treated as explicit engineering gaps and define the roadmap toward authorised field-data integration, calibration, improved thermal modelling, and eventual multi-well deployment. Keywords: Cyclic Steam Stimulation (CSS); Sucker-Rod Pumping (SRP); Heavy Oil; Digital Twin; Physics-Informed Modelling; Well-to-Surface Optimization; Scenario Simulation; Constrained Optimization; Uncertainty Quantification; Decision Support; Artificial Lift; Thermal Recovery; Smart Oilfield.

papers.title: Low-energy adaptive model predictive control of integrated EV thermal management system
papers.abstract: Electric vehicle thermal management systems suffer from high energy consumption, insufficient temperature control accuracy, and difficulties in multi-objective coordination, which have become critical bottlenecks restricting the improvement of driving range and vehicle performance. This paper proposes an integrated thermal management strategy combining a novel highly integrated eight-way valve architecture and adaptive variable-weight model predictive control (AMPC). A multi-physics coupled simulation platform is established, and eight full-condition adaptive operation modes are developed to support the development of precise control algorithms. An optimal temperature optimization method for batteries is presented to balance electric energy gain and heating energy consumption. An adaptive cost-function weight mechanism is developed to address the core limitation of conventional fixed-weight MPC that cannot adapt to complex operating conditions, thereby realizing the global optimization of thermal comfort, battery health and energy consumption. Multi-condition validation results demonstrate that the proposed AMPC strategy outperforms PID and traditional MPC in terms of higher temperature control accuracy, lower energy consumption and remarkable driving range improvement. Under extremely cold conditions, the battery temperature is raised from −13 °C to above 0 °C, with a maximum driving range increment of 22.7 km; under high-temperature summer conditions, the maximum driving range improvement reaches 34.5 km. The research outcomes provide control theories and engineering application solutions for electric vehicle thermal management, with good application and industrialization potential.

papers.title: Towards Suppressed Microstructural Anisotropy and Superior Mechanical Properties in Additively Manufactured Ti5553 Alloy Through Ta Doping
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) of near-β titanium alloys typically produces coarse columnar grains and strong <001> textures, which induce anisotropic mechanical behavior. Here, 5 wt.% tantalum (Ta) particles were doped into Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr (Ti-5553) powder to concurrently inhibit microstructural anisotropy and contribute to enhanced strength–ductility synergy via solidification modification. During the L-PBF process, unmelted Ta particles provided heterogeneous nucleation sites, while dissolved Ta generated local constitutional undercooling. Together, these effects reduced the average β-grain size from 47.23 ± 27.5 to 12.28 ± 11.8 μm and weakened the <001> texture, as well as increased yield strength from 870 to 990 MPa while retaining 28% elongation. After solution treatment and aging, Ti-5553-Ta reached a yield strength of 1196 MPa and 16.0% elongation. Local Ta-enriched precipitate-free zones and refined α precipitates contributed to the improved post-treatment ductility.

papers.title: Harnessing Physics-Informed Neural Network for advanced thermal management: Radiative MHD flow of hybrid CNTs past a stretching cylinder with Stefan blowing
papers.abstract: This article presents the thermal transport characteristics of the MHD Darcy–Forchheimer flow of Casson hybrid carbon nanotubes (HCNTs) over a stretching cylinder with radiation, viscous dissipation, endothermic/exothermic chemical reaction, heat consumption, Stefan blowing and zero mass flux condition. This investigation is motivated by the emerging demand to optimize thermal control in heat exchange devices, cooling thermal equipment, turbines, chemical synthesis and energy conversion processes. The hybrid CNTs can be created by the suspension of SWCNTs (Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes) and MWCNTs (Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes) in water. In addition, the non-Fourier heat and mass flux theory is incorporated in energy and nanofluid concentration expressions. The system of nonlinear ODEs derived through the implementation of the suitable transformations on the fundamental expressions. These equations are computed by employing the PINN (Physics-Informed Neural Network) and bvp4c solver. The PINN consist of a feed-forward network with one input layer, three hidden layers and one output layer for velocity, temperature and NF concentration profiles. It is trained with 10000 epochs, learning rate of 1 0 − 3 and Adam optimizer. An ANFIS (Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System) model proposed with suzeno type, 30 Gaussian membership function and 1000 epochs. The proposed PINN and ANFIS model achieve accuracy with R 2 values is close to 1 . The research outcomes demonstrate that the magnetic field and porosity parameters create a negative effect in the flow velocity profile and a positive effect in the temperature profile. The curvature parameter decline the thermal transfer gradient values. The findings of our research may have applications in many sectors, like drug delivery, cooling electrical equipment, tumour treatments and heat exchangers.

papers.title: From Trial-and-Error to Closed-Loop Design: A Data-Driven Review on Biomass-Derived Carbon for Supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Supercapacitors are vital for sustainable energy storage, and biomass-derived carbons are promising electrode materials owing to their low cost, renewability, and inherent hierarchical porosity. However, their electrochemical performance arises from a complex interplay of pore architecture, graphitization degree, and heteroatom doping, making trial-and-error optimization inefficient. This review adopts a data-driven perspective, systematically covering the entire value chain (from precursor selection and carbonization to pore engineering, surface modification, and characterization) while emphasizing how each variable can be quantified as input features for machine learning (ML). We discuss the mechanistic roles of structure, graphitization, and surface chemistry in regulating ion transport, electron conduction, and charge storage, and summarize common characterization (Raman, XRD, XPS, FTIR, BET) and electrochemical (CV, GCD, EIS) techniques. Critically, we highlight several problematic practices: the misleading “green” activation narrative, scalability limits of templating, non-linear trade-offs in chasing ultra-high surface area and heavy doping, oversimplified interpretation of the Raman I D / I G ratio, and deceptive reliance on three-electrode data for device-level predictions. To overcome these, we advocate for a closed-loop, data-driven design framework that integrates standardized databases, active learning, and inverse design to guide the rational development of biomass-derived carbon electrodes. This framework integrates ML not as an add-on but as the central engine connecting precursor–process–structure–performance relationships. Realizing the full potential of biomass-derived carbons demands a cultural shift from pursuing idealized metrics toward reproducibility, scalability, and rigorous device-relevant validation. By merging closed-loop data-driven discovery with mechanistic understanding, the field can effectively bridge the gap between laboratory findings and practical supercapacitor technologies.

papers.title: Stages of implementation of the process control system at the NPP based on the predictive analytics model
papers.abstract: The article discusses the stages of development and implementation of a process control system at nuclear power plants (NPPs) based on Model Predictive Control (MPC) predictive analytics models. The authors propose a comprehensive approach that integrates Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies, digital twins, predictive diagnostics, and intelligent operator support within the framework of the digital transformation of the nuclear industry. Particular attention is paid to the sequential execution of stages: equipping equipment with smart sensors, developing digital twins, implementing predictive analytics based on machine learning methods (specifically, MSET), and integrating MPC models to optimize real-time control. Case studies of applying this approach to specific power block systems (essential service water supply, reactor coolant pump oil supply, and power output) are considered. The final stage presents the development of an Operator Information Support System (OISS) that provides forecast visualization, decision explanation, and cognitive load reduction. In conclusion, it is emphasized that the implementation of MPC models contributes to increasing the safety, reliability, and economic efficiency of NPPs. The application of end-to-end predictive models based on machine learning methods allows the nuclear industry to systematically transition from reactive maintenance strategies to proactive management. Practical operational references of similar information support systems at the Novovoronezh NPP-2 power units clearly confirm the viability of this approach, demonstrating a reduction in the number of false trips of technological protections by more than twenty percent. Thus, linking predictive analytics with the MPC loop establishes a reliable mathematical foundation for verifying the design lifetime and justifying the safety of NPP elements in the long term.

papers.title: Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Real-Time Voltage Stability Margin Prediction under Renewable Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a Physics-Guided Transformer (PG-Transformer) framework that integrates physical knowledge of power systems with advanced deep learning architectures for accurate and uncertainty-aware VSM prediction. Simulated Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) measurements generated from dynamic time-domain simulations of the benchmark IEEE 39-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems are preprocessed using denoising, normalization and time windowing techniques to form a multivariate time series dataset. Classical stability indices L-index, Thevenin Equivalent Ratio and PV Margin are embedded into the learning pipeline to guide the model toward physically consistent feature representations. To address severe class imbalance, a Conditional Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (CWGAN-GP) is employed to generate synthetic unstable samples while maintaining physical validity. The proposed PG-Transformer employs multi-head self-attention for spatiotemporal correlation learning and Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty quantification. Experimental results show that the model achieves an RMSE of 0.0378, R² of 0.973, accuracy of 96.67%, F1-score of 0.886, and AUC of 0.987, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines such as Random Forest, CNN-LSTM and Physics-Guided LSTM models. Ablation studies confirm the complementary benefits of physics-guided features, GAN-based resampling, and uncertainty modeling, collectively improving accuracy by 6.47%. The framework operates with an average inference latency of 1.75 ms/sample, validating its suitability for real-time voltage stability monitoring in renewable-rich smart grids.

papers.title: Exact chiral symmetry, non-Hermiticity, and the axial anomaly on the lattice: A symmetry-class criterion for disorder-induced undoubling
papers.abstract: A lattice Dirac operator built to keep chiral symmetry exact by weighting the derivative with a quenched random field, the chiral disordered fermions, CDF, of [L. Jacobs, Phys. Rev. Lett. 51, 172 (1983)], is reexamined with tools unavailable when it was first formulated. We show that the disorder-averaged operator satisfiesB {Deff,N35}= 0B exactly, to all orders in the disorder strength: the disorder lifts the doubler degeneracy, pushing the doublers off the real axis into a complex (imaginary) mass while the physical mode stays exactly protected, yet it does so through non-Hermiticity rather than a Ginsparg--Wilson relation. As a consequence its axial index vanishes through every available channel: the Hermitian trace $Tr(\gfive D)$ (Karsten--Smit; Tiburzi), the bi-orthogonal index for non-Hermitian operators (Guo, Ma, and Zhang), and, closing the last loophole, the algebraic (Riesz-projector) index even when the operator is defective at an exceptional point. The CDF operator therefore cannot reproduce the axial anomaly, not by a tunable near-miss but by an identity forced by the very chiral symmetry it preserves. We organize this and the neighboring constructions by the Dirac channel that carries the lattice structure: disorder in the $\g_\mu$ (chirality-preserving) channel realizes an Altland--Zirnbauer chiral class and can never carry an index, while disorder in the $\mathbb{1}$ (mass) channel breaks chiral symmetry and reproduces Callan--Harvey / domain-wall physics. A one-parameter family interpolates between the two, with the index a step function of the engaged channel: the 1983 operator and Kaplan's domain wall emerge as the two poles of a single disordered family, distinguished not by the disorder but by the channel that carries it. The picture unifies the lattice-QCD undoubling lineage with the tenfold-way classification of disordered Dirac fermions, and settles the fate of the disorder route to chiral lattice fermions.

papers.title: Adaptive wavelet-CNN-LSTM forecasting with Bayesian optimization and SHAP interpretability for short-term solar irradiance prediction in a hot arid climate
papers.abstract: Abstract Short-term global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting is essential for solar grid integration in hot arid sites due to atmospheric variability and dust aerosols. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning (DL) pipeline that combines Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers for 15-min GHI forecasting at a site in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Wavelet decomposition and model hyperparameters are jointly optimized using Optuna’s Bayesian search across 20 trials, and SHAP-based feature selection retains only the most informative predictors. Uncertainty is quantified through Monte Carlo dropout across 100 stochastic forward passes with a dropout rate of 0.2. The model is evaluated on 105,312 meteorological records using five-fold time-series cross-validation. Across all observations, the model achieves a mean RMSE of 6.62 ± 2.22 W/m 2 and an R 2 of 0.98 ± 0.01. Daytime-filtered evaluation (GHI > 50 W/m 2 ) yields a mean RMSE of 8.28 ± 1.45 W/m 2 and an R 2 of 0.961 ± 0.015, providing a more conservative estimate of forecasting accuracy during operationally relevant periods. The full pipeline reduces RMSE by 28–40% compared to ablated model variants and achieves a 47% reduction compared to the persistence baseline. The proposed pipeline delivers interpretable solar irradiance forecasting with calibrated uncertainty estimates suited for grid management applications at arid-climate sites.

papers.title: Mean-based hesitant fuzzy spaces with an application to medical prediagnosis
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in intelligent decision-support systems frequently arises from heterogeneous, multi-source, and linguistically expressed information. Hesitant fuzzy sets (HFSs) provide a flexible representation of such uncertainty by allowing multiple possible membership degrees for a single element. However, most existing HFS-based models operate at the membership level and lack a unified space-level structure to organize hesitant information within a consistent compositional framework. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a mean-based hesitant fuzzy space that includes a refined mean-induced total ordering along with its corresponding lattice structure. The proposed framework establishes a structured ambient domain in which hesitant fuzzy elements can be consistently compared, aggregated, and manipulated. Mean lattices and mean M -sublattices are developed to support order-theoretic operations, and hesitant fuzzy subspaces are formalized with corresponding structural properties. To demonstrate its practical relevance, the proposed hesitant fuzzy space is integrated into a medical prediagnosis pipeline. Hesitant clinical assessments are encoded within the mean-based lattice, transformed into lattice-consistent numerical features, and then used as inputs to a Nearest Centroid classifier. This pipeline is illustrated with a worked numerical example designed to make each computational step transparent and verifiable; it serves as a proof-of-concept demonstration rather than an empirical evaluation on real clinical data. The proposed framework provides a coherent mathematical foundation for uncertainty-aware intelligent systems and offers a flexible, scalable machine-learning-ready feature representation layer for future classification and decision-support applications.

papers.title: PHYSICS-INFORMED DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR INTELLIGENT FAULT PREDICTION AND REMAINING USEFUL LIFE ESTIMATION OF ROTATING MACHINERY
papers.abstract: Unexpected failures in rotating machinery may lead to large economic losses and even safety problems. Accurately predictingremaining useful life (RUL) plays an important role in equipment maintenance. Because of the strong non-linearity and noisesensitivity of data-driven models, however, their interpretation is often limited, and it is challenging to incorporate physicaldegradation mechanisms and achieve generalization. This article proposes a Prior-Information and Physics-Informed NeuralNetwork framework for intelligent RUL prediction of rotating machinery. The framework follows a cloud-edge collaborativeparadigm, where vibration signals are firstly processed by an improved particle filter based on a Damage DiscrepancyAccumulation Hypothesis at the edge to extract degradation features, and then Prior-Weighted Self-Attention is applied in thecloud to capture richer features of the degradation process by introducing the perturbation-based prior information. Finally, aFast-Slow Coupling Physics-Informed Neural Network is adopted to fully utilize the physical degradation knowledge for makingthe model more interpretable. The experimental results on a public data set and a self-built rotating-machinery test rig show theeffectiveness of the proposed paradigm in achieving higher accuracy than existing approaches. Moreover, the framework achievesgood performance even under noisy conditions. The work demonstrates the value of using prior information, vibrationdegradation features, and physical knowledge to enable rotating-machinery prognostics with high accuracy and interpretation.
